content:
The atmosphere around Meta AI glasses has been a bit off lately. The situation has gotten so bad that one of today's top three paid apps on the iPhone is an application specifically designed to detect whether people nearby are wearing smart glasses.

This app makes no pretense about its purpose—it's called the "Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner." It claims to be able to detect whether someone around you is wearing Meta AI glasses, and then send you a notification.

Enough iPhone users are willing to spend $3 to try out this app that it now ranks 3rd on the US iPhone paid App Store charts. It's extremely rare for new paid apps to break into this ranking.

We haven't tested whether this app actually works, and even if it does detect someone wearing AI glasses, you wouldn't know what to do about it.

Smart glasses equipped with cameras are still relatively easy to spot right now, so you don't actually need an app to notice when someone is wearing them.

Still, the sentiment is clear: plenty of people feel uneasy about the concept of AI smart glasses, seeing privacy issues involved. If Apple wants to join the smart glasses fray next year, this could be said to be a significant obstacle.
